action.health.battery-report.desc: Runs powercfg /batteryreport and saves battery-report.html in the WinCare reports folder: design vs current capacity, cycles and usage history. Read-only; on a PC without a battery powercfg reports that there is none.
action.health.energy-report.desc: Runs powercfg /energy for 60 seconds and saves energy-report.html in the reports folder: power-efficiency problems, devices and programs that prevent sleep. Requires administrator and takes about 1 minute; leave the PC idle while it measures.
action.health.reliability-open.desc: Opens Windows Reliability Monitor (perfmon /rel) with the timeline of application, Windows and install failures. Nothing is changed.
action.health.export-events.desc: Saves to JSON, in the reports folder, the summary of critical events and application crashes of the last 7 days (counts, sources, IDs and dates). Event message text is not included.
section.health.critical-events.note: Unexpected shutdowns (Kernel-Power 41, EventLog 6008), blue screens (BugCheck 1001), disk and NTFS errors (disk 7/11/51/153, Ntfs 55/98) and hardware errors (WHEA) in the last 7 days, grouped by source and ID. Message text is not read.
section.health.app-crashes.note: Programs that crashed or hung in the last 7 days. One crash usually produces an Application Error 1000 event and a Windows Error Reporting 1001 report, so both counts are shown separately.
section.health.devices.note: Devices with a Device Manager error code. Disabled (22) and not connected (45) are usually choices or normal states. WinCare does not change drivers.
section.health.disks.note: Health reported by the disk itself (Get-PhysicalDisk) and reliability counters (wear, temperature, uncorrected errors). The counters usually require administrator.
section.health.startup-tasks.note: Tasks outside \Microsoft\ that run at sign-in or at boot. Information only: WinCare does not disable tasks.
section.health.startup-services.note: Automatic-start services whose executable is outside the Windows folder and not signed by Microsoft. Information only: WinCare does not change services.
section.health.battery.note: Design (factory) capacity vs current full-charge capacity. Wear above 40% usually reduces battery life noticeably.
section.health.updates.note: Read-only: date of the last install and whether a restart is pending. WinCare never changes, pauses or resets Windows Update.
section.health.time-uptime.note: Time since the last restart and the configured time synchronization source. A wrong clock breaks sign-in, certificates and updates.
section.health.battery.none: No battery found (desktop, server or virtual machine).
section.health.unavailable: This section could not be collected. See the page errors.

finding.health-bugchecks.title: {0} blue screen(s) in the last {1} days
finding.health-bugchecks.recommendation: Check the stop code in Critical events and in Reliability Monitor. Update drivers from the manufacturer and test memory (Windows Memory Diagnostic).
finding.health-disk-errors.title: {0} disk or NTFS error(s) in the last {1} days
finding.health-disk-errors.recommendatio: Back up important data now. Run the online disk scan (chkdsk /scan) on the Integrity page and check disk health on this page.
finding.health-unexpected-shutdowns.titl: {0} unexpected shutdown(s) in the last {1} days
finding.health-unexpected-shutdowns.reco: Common causes: power loss, holding the power button, overheating or a failing power supply. If there was no power loss, check temperature and power supply.
finding.health-whea-errors.title: {0} hardware error(s) (WHEA) in the last {1} days
finding.health-whea-errors.recommendatio: WHEA errors come from the CPU, memory or PCIe bus. Update BIOS/UEFI and chipset drivers; if they persist, contact the manufacturer's support.
finding.health-disk-unhealthy.title: Disk {0} reports a health problem
finding.health-disk-unhealthy.recommenda: Back up immediately and plan to replace the disk. Do not run defragmentation or heavy repairs before the backup.
finding.health-device-problems.title: {0} device(s) with a driver error
finding.health-device-problems.recommend: See the code and meaning in the Devices section. Install the manufacturer's driver or use Device Manager; WinCare does not change drivers.
finding.health-battery-worn.title: Battery is {0}% worn
finding.health-battery-worn.recommendati: Generate the Battery report to see the history. Above 40% battery life drops noticeably; consider a replacement from the manufacturer.
finding.health-update-stale.title: No update installed for {0} days
finding.health-update-stale.recommendati: Open Settings > Windows Update and check. In a company, contact IT: WinCare does not touch Windows Update.
finding.health-uptime-long.title: Computer running for {0} days without a restart
finding.health-uptime-long.recommendatio: Restart when you can: updates and drivers only finish after a restart, and it often clears accumulated slowness.
finding.health-clock.title: The computer clock looks wrong
finding.health-clock.recommendation: Check date, time and time zone in Settings > Time & language. A wrong clock breaks sign-in, certificates and updates.
